newsitem.title: USA: Archer warns Clinton against tax hikes in budget.
newsitem.headline: Archer warns Clinton against tax hikes in budget.

text.p: The chairman of the House tax-writing committee Saturday warned President Clinton against raising taxes to balance the budget and said any cuts he proposes should truly reduce the tax burden.

Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said it was unlikely Congress would pass a budget this year that did not include broad capital gains tax relief and urged the president to expand his plan which is expected to give relief only to homesellers.
In remarks prepared for delivery to the National Centre for Policy Analysis, Archer said Clinton's tax plan should not simply give a tax cut to one group and then pay for it with tax hikes on others.
"Common ground will more likely result if the president avoids temporary tax relief proposals and if he doesn't drown his tax cuts with tax hikes," Archer said.
The president's new budget which he will unveil Feb. 6 is expected to include around $100 billion in tax cuts over five years while bringing the federal budget in balance by 2002.
The Texas Republican has said he favours closing tax loopholes pending complete reform of the tax system to shift from an income tax to a consumption tax.
Clinton's rumoured plan to reduce the capital gains tax on profits from sales of homes should be expanded to other investments, Archer suggested.
"There is bipartisan recognition that earnings have already been taxed before becoming invested and therefore they should not be taxed again because they have appreciated in value," he said.
And, while Congress will take a close look at which tax loopholes can be closed, there is opposition to using this as a way to shift the tax burden to companies and investors, he said.
"Fiscal conservatism means balanced budgets and low taxes, not balanced budgets thanks to new taxes," Archer said.
